title: Firecrawl-compatible scrape over MCP and loopback REST, Windows fetch engine and contract harness

dependency_notes.SG-000131: Contracts v1, audit chain, licence gates and the FD-06 allowlist.
dependency_notes.SG-000040: Closed. The Windows WinHTTP transport, DNS pinning to the validated address set, exact-peer check and SSRF rules are reused unchanged by the fetch engine. Its note says no MCP network tool is registered; this grain amends that guard for exactly the tools listed below.
dependency_notes.SG-000064: Closed. Admitted web_fetch as a local-only MCP tool; the same guard tests are amended here.
dependency_notes.SG-000108: Closed. Governed navigation (SG-000075), extraction and the test-only fixture pinning that the chromium engine and the harness reuse.
dependency_notes.SG-000122: Closed. Browser form shapes stay as they are; this grain adds none.

packets: WP1-07 (web_scrape, REST scrape routes, REST tokens, guard amendment)
objective: Let a local caller on Windows scrape one public HTTPS page through the Firecrawl v2 contract (with a v1 alias) using the MIT Firecrawl SDKs unchanged, via the MCP tool web_scrape (capability web, operation scrape) or the loopback REST route POST /v2/scrape authenticated by a per-client REST token, with orceld as the sole authority. Two engines: fetch (the existing Windows SG-000040 transport, then HTML to Markdown in the contained orcel-doc-parser) and chromium (the existing browser host's extract_page, in live-browser-dev and live-browser-test builds). macOS and Linux report every web entry unsupported until WP2-12 and SG-000115. The result and audit name the engine that ran. The contract is reimplemented in Apache-2.0 code from the MIT SDK types; no AGPL Firecrawl file is copied or vendored, and existing FD-06 files are unchanged.

include: crates/orcel-web (depends on orcel-contracts only): v2 and v1 scrape request types derived from the MIT SDK types, refusal by name of every unsupported field, translation to RequestEnvelope with front-supplied Ids, Document shaping (section 5.3 of the spec).

orceld: capability web/scrape with engines fetch (Windows) and chromium; capability report entries per OS and build; one SOFT approval per scrape bound to URL, engine, formats, resolved-address-set digest and orcel_session_id; TARGET_STALE on address drift; audit of the engine that ran.

apps/orcel-mcp: tool_contract entry web_scrape (local_only, effect network, approval SOFT); loopback routes POST /v2/scrape and POST /v1/scrape on the existing loopback server with its bind, Host, Origin and body checks; REST tokens (orcel_rest_ prefix, hashed at rest, per-client principal, rotation and removal through the local control path) distinct from the MCP token; network-tool guard tests amended to admit exactly the eight web tools of the spec.
orcel-lifecycle: orcel client add-rest, rotate-rest and remove-rest; emitted client configs always set apiUrl explicitly and refuse to omit it.
apps/orcel-doc-parser: format html, sniffed and refused when not HTML, using html5ever =0.40.1 with an Orcel-owned tree sink; a Rust port of Orcel's own worker extraction.
tests/firecrawl-compat: @mendable/firecrawl-js 4.54.0 and firecrawl-py 4.57.0 (CI only) as black-box contract clients against the pinned fixture site; parity report per matrix row.
exclude: Any new AGPL Firecrawl code or file, including apps/api/openapi.json; FD-06 files stay as they are.
Any network transport on macOS or Linux (WP2-12, FD-UP-12).
Remote (relay or OAuth) exposure of the new tools.
Formats screenshot, json, summary and the other rows marked later or not planned in section 5.3; actions; custom headers (FD-UP-8); skipTlsVerification; stealth proxy, mobile and location (FD-UP-2).
Any change to existing browser_* shapes, their profiles or their approvals.
The chromium engine in release builds (development-only until F4 slice 7 is decided); the fetch engine in release builds unless FD-UP-7 allows it.

authority_delta.web_scrape: Proposed: a new local-only capability web/scrape that composes existing governed paths (the SG-000040 Windows transport and SG-000075 navigation) behind one SOFT approval per request. No new network class or transport, no listener beyond the existing loopback server, no persistent profile.
authority_delta.mcp_network_guard: Proposed: the SG-000040/SG-000064 network-tool guard admits exactly web_scrape, web_map, web_crawl_start, web_batch_scrape_start, web_job_status, web_job_cancel, web_job_errors and web_job_list (the last seven owned by SG-000102).
authority_delta.rest_tokens: Proposed: per-client REST tokens minted only from the local control path; they authenticate a client principal and grant no authority beyond the tools' own approvals.

decisions.question: Firecrawl approach
decisions.status: PENDING (FD-UP-1); this draft assumes option (a), reimplementation in Apache-2.0 code

decisions.question: Fetch engine in Windows release builds

invariants: orceld remains the sole authority; the loopback REST front and the MCP edge decide nothing.
No new AGPL-marked file enters crates/, apps/, packages/ or tests/; only docs/orcel/notices/fd06-files.txt paths may carry AGPL markers.
Every refused or unsupported option is refused before any dispatch, by name.
A scrape never runs on an engine other than the one reported in its result and audit event; a fallback is reported, never silent.
The HTML parser runs with no network and no process creation under orcel-contain.
The MCP token is refused on REST routes and a REST token on /mcp.
Safe-mode approvals for every pre-existing shape are unchanged.
acceptance: Every W1 scrape row of the parity matrix passes the JS and Python SDK harness on Windows with both engines; on Linux and macOS the harness asserts UNSUPPORTED.
Every refused field of section 5.3 has a test and surfaces as the SDK's typed error.
The fetch engine's Markdown matches the worker extraction on shared fixtures within the documented normalisation.
An approval cannot be replayed after the address set changes (TARGET_STALE) or after a restart.
REST token rotation invalidates the old token immediately; the emitted client config always sets apiUrl.
A fresh-context security judge passes WP1-06 and WP1-07.
